title: We should all appreciate vultures more!
description:
From memes to movies, we’ve all seen vultures getting a bit of a bad rep! The bird of prey is often linked to death and decay, but some people are trying to fight back and try and give them a bit of a rebrand.

Kojo Baidoo is a vulture fan and birder in the US. He tells us about how he’s trying to rehab the vulture brand through social media and why we should have some more love for these feathered friends.

Plus, Makuochi Okafor our West Africa reporter, explains how vultures are disappearing in Nigeria, but a man called the ‘Vulture King’ is trying to save them.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討大眾對禿鷹的偏見、禿鷹的重要生態價值，以及其在奈及利亞等地的保育挑戰。美國鳥類愛好者 Kojo Baidoo 分享了他如何透過社群媒體影片改善禿鷹形象，並指出禿鷹具有良好的社交與照顧家庭習性，其強大的胃酸能分解炭疽桿菌與狂犬病等病原體，是生態系中預防疾病傳播的關鍵防線。BBC 西非記者 Makuochi Okafor 則指出，西非與奈及利亞的禿鷹因被視為不祥之兆，甚至遭捕殺用於傳統信仰儀式而大量減少；雖然有被稱為 Vulture King 的在地居民與保育人士合作保護牠們，但各國政府與專家仍需加強跨國執法以打擊非法貿易。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World examines why vultures carry a negative reputation and highlights efforts to rebrand and protect them. Kojo Baidoo, a US bird enthusiast and researcher, explains how he uses social media to show vultures' caring social nature and their crucial role as nature's clean-up crew, noting that their powerful stomach acid destroys deadly pathogens like anthrax and rabies. Meanwhile, BBC West Africa reporter Makuochi Okafor discusses the steep decline of vultures in Nigeria and West Africa, where they are hunted for belief-based ritual practices and viewed as bad omens. Despite local protection efforts led by a community member known as the 'Vulture King,' experts and governments are pushing for stronger cross-border enforcement to curb illegal trade and save threatened species.
